content: Synthetic Computers at Scale for Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation 1 Introduction 2 Synthetic Computer Creation 2.1 Persona-Driven User Profiles 2.2 Computer Environment Planning 2.2.1 Filesystem Policy Generation 2.2.2 Filesystem Planning 2.3 Artifact Creation 3 Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation 3.1 Setup 3.1.1 Productivity Objectives 3.1.2 Collaboration Setup 3.2 Planning and Daily Work Simulation 4 Experiments 4.1 Experimental Setup 4.2 Results 4.2.1 Final Deliverable Evaluation 4.2.2 Full Trajectory Analysis 4.3 In-Domain Evaluation 4.4 Out-of-Domain Evaluation 5 Discussion 5.1 Toward Self-Improving Productivity Agents 5.2 Scaling with Simulation and Model Capability 5.3 Toward Scalable Productive Intelligence 6 Conclusion and Future Work References A Retrospective Analysis Report License: CC BY 4.0 arXiv:2604.28181v1 [cs.AI] 30 Apr 2026 Synthetic Computers at Scale for Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation Tao Ge , Baolin Peng , Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao Microsoft {taoge, baolinpeng}@microsoft.com huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/synthetic-computers-at-scale Abstract Realistic long-horizon productivity work is strongly conditioned on user-specific computer environments, where much of the work context is stored and organized through directory structures and content-rich artifacts. To scale synthetic data creation for such productivity scenarios, we introduce Synthetic Computers at Scale, a scalable methodology for creating such environments with realistic folder hierarchies and content-rich artifacts (e.g., documents, spreadsheets, and presentations).
